category_title: Preschoolers with disruptive behaviors maintained by attention and escape
minimal_context: Delon is participating in a preschool circle time activity where the teacher is reading a book and asking students questions.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, let's sit in our circle. I am going to open our circle time book and begin to read.

STUDENT: (Makes an animal noise and starts shouting) I can’t see the book!

TUTOR: Please sit still and be quiet.

STUDENT: (Shouts) This is boring! (Hums a song and pretends to touch the peer sitting in front of him)

TUTOR: Let's keep reading. Now, I am going to ask another student a question. Sarah, what do you think happens next?

STUDENT: (Touches the peer sitting next to him, then hits the peer)

options.A: Provide the student with a kit comprising assorted coloring sheets, art materials, and crayons to use independently during the circle time activity.
options.B: Require the student to remain in the circle time activity until the end of the session, providing only quick, brief redirections for disruptions to minimize attention.
options.C: Provide the student with a pressure vest as a sensory accommodation to wear for the remainder of the circle time activity.
options.D: Help the student reflect on the consequences of his actions and the emotions of the peer he hit (for example, by saying, 'He is sad because...').
